entries.process_causes: Gas entrapment from dissolved gases not escaping before solidification; excessive moisture in mold sand; inadequate venting; pouring temperature too low, trapping gas.
Insufficient feeding during solidification; poor riser design/placement; cooling rate too fast in thick sections; inadequate directional solidification.
Two streams of molten metal meeting without fully fusing; pouring temperature too low; slow pouring rate; poor gating design causing metal to cool before merging.
Excessive shrinkage stress during solidification; mold too rigid, restricting contraction; incorrect alloy composition increasing hot-shortness; uneven cooling rates.
Sand or slag entrapped in the metal during pouring; poor filtration; mold erosion during filling; dirty molten metal.
Metal solidified before completely filling the mold; pouring temperature too low; insufficient metal fluidity; gating system too restrictive.
Sand mold surface too coarse; excessive pouring temperature causing sand-metal reaction; inadequate mold coating.
Excess metal escaping at the mold parting line; worn or poorly clamped mold halves; excessive pouring pressure.
Uneven cooling rates across the part; residual stress from asymmetric wall thickness; premature mold removal.
